title: Bounded finite-presentation flat proper cohomology model on a fixed affine open
statement: Let f:X→T be proper, locally of finite presentation and quasi-compact. Assume X.Modules has injective resolutions, and F is a finitely presented O_X-module flat over f [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. For every open U⊆T such that U.toScheme is affine, there exist a complex B of O_U-modules [def-pc-derived-category] and b∈ℕ with B concentrated in [0,b], each term flat over U, quasi-coherent and finitely presented. For any g:T′→U and cartesian square X′→X over T′→T, assuming injective resolutions on X′, H^q(g*B) is isomorphic to R^q f′_*(g′*F) for every q∈ℕ. No degree bound or prior cohomology model is supplied.

source.place: Tags 0B91(2), 0A1H (proper perfect direct image by Noetherian approximation), 08EB (affine model), 0653 (flat opcycle); 068V (lower residue-field Tor bound)

proof.text: Restrict f and F to the affine U by the standard pullback. Properness, finite presentation and relative flatness survive base change. Apply the proper-support perfect-direct-image theorem with E=O and G=F in degree zero: every term has proper support because f is proper. The theorem makes K=Rf_*F perfect and compatible with every base change. Its Noetherian approximation proof is exactly the geometric step of the coherence unit, not an alternative route.

Identify U with Spec Γ(U,O). The affine characterization represents K by a bounded finite-projective ring complex. Every derived fibre is the cohomology of the pulled-back F in degree zero and has no negative cohomology. The lower Tor bound is zero. Choose a bounded-above finite free representative, and replace its negative tail by the degree-zero opcycle. Negative tensor-homology vanishing gives flatness of that opcycle; it is finitely presented, hence projective. This gives a finite-projective representative in [0,b], with b enlarged to a natural number. The finite free complex is only an auxiliary representative, not a claim of global freeness of the truncated complex.

Associate sheaves to the ring complex and transport along U≅Spec Γ(U,O). Its terms are finitely presented, flat and quasi-coherent. These bounded flat complexes calculate derived pullback by ordinary pullback. Take homology of the derived base-change comparison to obtain the stated higher-direct-image isomorphisms, globally for every new base. A supplied arbitrary pullback square is canonically isomorphic to the standard fibre product; transport the comparison along that isomorphism. If U or its inverse image is empty, take B=0 and b=0.
